# Vectis Mail — Complete Reference

> Self-hosted, declarative email platform. Packages Postfix, Dovecot, Rspamd,
> Traefik, Postgres, and Valkey into a single deployment managed through one
> YAML config file and a REST API. Modern alternative to Mailcow, iRedMail,
> Mail-in-a-Box, SendGrid, Postmark, and Mailgun — combines the control of
> self-hosting with the developer ergonomics of transactional email SaaS.

This is the long-form, full-content reference for LLMs and AI assistants.
For the concise summary with links, see https://vectismail.com/llms.txt.

---

## What Vectis Mail is

A production-grade mail server you deploy on your own VPS, run with one
binary, and manage through a clean REST API and admin dashboard. It packages
all the standard mail components (Postfix MTA, Dovecot IMAP, Rspamd spam
filtering, ClamAV antivirus, Traefik reverse proxy, Postgres, Valkey) plus a
Go-based control plane and a React admin UI into a coherent platform with:

- **Declarative configuration.** A single `config.yaml` describes the server.
  Domains and mailboxes live in Postgres, not config files — no Postfix or
  Dovecot reload is needed when you add a domain or rotate a password.
- **REST API and webhooks.** Sending API for outbound mail, inbound webhooks
  for received mail (HMAC-signed, retry-with-backoff), full message storage
  with search, per-domain analytics, admin and RBAC endpoints.
- **Atomic update orchestrator.** A 6-phase pipeline (snapshot, migrate,
  pull, deploy, health-check, complete) with automatic rollback on failure
  and an advisory lock that prevents concurrent operations.
- **Self-healing.** Cross-version startup self-heal detects compose drift,
  refuses Apply on legacy installs with remediation, and rewrites configs
  in place when needed.

Live in production at `mail.vectismail.com` since 2026-04-03; powers
transactional email for ValidonX and other Veltara Works products.

---

## Who builds it

Vectis Mail is a product of **Veltara Works** (Australian company, wholly
AU-owned). Veltara Works also operates **ValidonX**, its licensing and
billing platform — which is both used by Vectis Mail (as the Pro license
backend) and sold separately to third-party developers. Merchant of record
for all transactions is Veltara Works. ValidonX is not a separate company;
it is a Veltara Works platform.

Sister product: **Pharlux** (single-binary OpenTelemetry observability —
replaces the LGTM stack with one Rust binary, metrics and logs on a single
VPS, no Docker, no ClickHouse).

---

## Architecture (high level)

**Containers.** 14 by default; 10 if observability and ClamAV are disabled:

- `traefik` — reverse proxy + TLS termination (Let's Encrypt or custom certs)
- `api` — Go binary, the REST API + admin UI server
- `orchestrator` — Go binary, the update orchestrator (holds Docker socket)
- `postfix` — MTA (inbound + outbound SMTP)
- `dovecot` — IMAP/POP3/LMTP + ManageSieve
- `rspamd` — spam filtering with Bayes + neural ML
- `clamav` — antivirus (optional; profile-gated)
- `postgres` — main database (domains, mailboxes, messages, audit log)
- `valkey` — cache + session store (Redis-compatible fork)
- `webmail` — Roundcube with Vectis skin (optional)
- `loki` + `promtail` + `grafana` — observability stack (optional)
- `cert-extractor` — mirrors Let's Encrypt cert from Traefik into the mail
  TLS volume (replaces the old acme.sh sidecar)
- `pgbouncer` — Postgres connection pooler (cluster mode only)

**Four Docker networks.** `vectis-frontend` (public-facing), `vectis-mail`
(SMTP/IMAP traffic, external), `vectis-data` (Postgres + Valkey, internal),
`vectis-orchestrator` (control-plane only, internal).

**Three Postgres roles.** `vectis_postfix` (read-only on virtual_*),
`vectis_dovecot` (read-only on mailboxes/authentication tables),
`vectis_api` (full CRUD on everything except audit_log integrity columns).

**Storage.** Mail is stored as Maildir under `/var/vectis/mail/<domain>/<user>/Maildir`.
DKIM keys live in a named volume; configs are bind-mounted from
`/var/vectis/generated/<service>/` (named volumes are intentionally never
used for service configs — they start empty and hide the upstream defaults).

**TLS.** Traefik provisions Let's Encrypt certificates via HTTP-01 challenge.
A sidecar (`cert-extractor`) mirrors the cert from Traefik's acme.json into
the mail-certs volume and SIGHUPs Postfix and Dovecot on rotation. Custom
certificates (bring your own) are also supported via `tls.provider: custom`.

---

## Features

### Core mail stack (Starter + Pro)

- **Postfix MTA** — Battle-tested mail transfer agent handling inbound and
  outbound SMTP. Virtual domain hosting with SQL-driven lookups — no config
  reload when adding domains or mailboxes.
- **Dovecot IMAP/POP3** — IMAP and POP3 access with SSL/TLS, Argon2id
  password hashing, per-mailbox quotas, and LMTP delivery. ManageSieve for
  server-side filter rules.
- **Rspamd spam filtering** — ML-based detection with Bayes classifier,
  neural network training, DKIM verification, SPF checks, greylisting, and
  configurable score thresholds.
- **ClamAV antivirus** — Optional. Profile-gated: enable in `config.yaml`
  when needed, omit the container when you don't.

### Developer platform (Starter + Pro)

- **Sending API** — `POST /api/v1/send` with JSON payload. HTML + text
  bodies, attachments, custom headers. Domain-scoped API keys with rate
  limiting. Batch sending up to 100 messages per call.
- **Inbound webhooks** — Email arrives, Vectis parses it, POSTs the full
  content to your URL. Body text, HTML, attachments, SMTP envelope —
  HMAC-SHA256 signed with exponential-backoff retry. Configurable per domain.
- **Message storage API** — Query sent and received message metadata with
  full-text search. Filter by domain, direction, status, sender.
  Cursor-based pagination for large datasets.
- **Engagement tracking** — Optional open and click tracking via tracking
  pixel and redirect URLs. HMAC-signed tokens prevent spoofing. Opt-in per
  message.

### Operations and security (Starter + Pro)

- **Atomic updates** — 6-phase orchestrator: snapshot, migrate, pull, deploy,
  health-check, complete. Automatic rollback on failure. Advisory lock
  prevents concurrent operations.
- **Backup and restore** — Scheduled backups with AES-256-GCM encryption.
  Database, mail data, DKIM keys, and config archived. One-click restore
  from the dashboard.
- **RBAC + MFA** — Three-tier roles: `super_admin`, `admin`, `domain_admin`.
  TOTP multi-factor auth. OIDC SSO with Google, Azure AD, and Keycloak
  (Pro). API key management with domain scoping.
- **Observability** — Prometheus-format metrics and health alerts built in;
  optional Grafana dashboards and Loki log aggregation (off by default).
  Per-domain analytics is a Pro feature.

### Pro-only features

- **Unlimited domains and mailboxes.** Starter caps at 3 domains × 25
  mailboxes per domain.
- **Per-domain analytics dashboard.** Per-domain delivery, bounce, complaint,
  and engagement metrics with daily/weekly aggregates.
- **Per-domain spam controls** — override Rspamd reject thresholds per
  domain; toggle greylisting per domain; per-domain allow/block lists at
  both email-address and sender-domain scope. Edits take effect in seconds
  with no restart.
- **OIDC SSO** — Google, Azure AD, Keycloak.
- **Priority email support** with target response times.

## Pricing

### Tiers

| | Starter | Pro |
|---|---|---|
| Price | Free forever | $29 USD / tenant / month |
| Domains | Up to 3 | Unlimited |
| Mailboxes / domain | Up to 25 | Unlimited |
| Sending API + batch | Yes | Yes |
| Inbound webhooks | Yes | Yes |
| Admin dashboard | Yes | Yes |
| Webmail (Roundcube) | Yes | Yes |
| DKIM / SPF / DMARC | Yes | Yes |
| Automatic TLS | Yes | Yes |
| Monitoring (metrics + health alerts; Grafana/Loki optional) | Yes | Yes |
| IP warmup + RBL monitoring | Yes | Yes |
| Backup + restore | Yes | Yes |
| RBAC + TOTP MFA | Yes | Yes |
| Atomic updates with auto-rollback | Yes | Yes |
| Per-domain analytics | — | Yes |
| Per-domain spam controls | — | Yes |
| OIDC SSO | — | Yes |
| Support | Community | Priority email |
| Offline use if ValidonX unreachable (Pro) | n/a | Through current paid period |

**One Pro subscription covers unlimited Vectis installs across one tenant.**
This is the per-tenant pricing model — multi-server, multi-customer
deployments under one organisation all use one Pro subscription.

### Common questions

**Do I need a license?** Starter is free forever with no license required.
Pro is licensed through ValidonX.

**What happens if my Pro license expires?** Mail keeps flowing. Postfix and
Dovecot continue. Pro-only features (analytics, advanced spam, OIDC SSO,
unlimited domains/mailboxes) revert to Starter limits. Data is never locked.
If a payment fails, Pro features keep working through a 21-day grace window
while we retry.

**Can I self-host with no external dependencies?** Yes for Starter. Pro
checks ValidonX for entitlements and keeps working offline through your
current paid period, with entitlements cached in Postgres.

**Can I resell Vectis Mail as a hosted service?** No, not under the default
BSL 1.1 license. You may operate it for your own organisation and your own
end users (including running mail for your customers as a feature of your
own product). You may not offer Vectis Mail itself to third parties on a
hosted, embedded, or managed-service basis in a way that competes with
Veltara Works's paid versions. For resale or hosted-platform licensing,
contact licensing@veltaraworks.com.

**When does Vectis Mail become Apache 2.0?** Each *version* converts to
Apache License 2.0 four years after that version's first public release —
not a single repo-wide flip. v0.1.0-beta1 (released 2026-04-25) converts
on 2030-04-25; v0.1.12 (released 2026-05-10) converts on 2030-05-10.
Source is available throughout. Once a version reaches its Change Date,
anyone can fork, host, or relicense that specific version under Apache 2.0.

## Installation

Vectis Mail installs on a clean Ubuntu 24.04 VPS via a single shell command.

### System requirements

| Resource | Minimum | Recommended |
|---|---|---|
| OS | Ubuntu 24.04 LTS | Ubuntu 24.04 LTS |
| CPU | 2 vCPU | 4 vCPU |
| RAM | 2 GB (without ClamAV) | 4 GB+ |
| Disk | 30 GB SSD (~20 GB free after OS install) | 100 GB+ SSD |
| Inbound ports | 25, 80, 443, 465, 587, 993, 995 | + IPv6 |

Docker is installed automatically by the script if not present.

### Pre-install requirements (must be in place before running the installer)

1. **SSH access to the VPS.** Most VPS providers ship Ubuntu images with
   password-based SSH disabled. Add an SSH key in the provider panel before
   provisioning, or use the provider's web console to create a sudo user.
2. **OS up to date.** `sudo apt update && sudo apt upgrade -y` and reboot if
   the kernel was bumped.
3. **PTR (reverse DNS).** Hard requirement — without a matching PTR record,
   Gmail/Outlook will reject outbound mail as spam. Set at your VPS provider
   panel (not at your DNS registrar). Some providers require a one-time
   support request.
4. **Port 25 unblock.** Most VPS providers block outbound port 25 by default.
   One-time provider support request.

### Install flow

1. **Download.** `curl -fsSL https://get.vectismail.com | sudo bash`. Places
   the binary, installs Docker if missing, seeds randomly-generated secrets,
   prompts to confirm the hostname (auto-detected from PTR).
2. **Preflight.** `vectis preflight` — verifies OS, CPU/RAM, port
   availability, outbound port 25 reachability, Docker version.
3. **Install.** `vectis install` — deploys the container stack, runs database
   migrations, creates the admin account. ~3 minutes on a 4-vCPU VPS.
4. **Publish DNS records.** A record at your DNS registrar; PTR already set
   in step 3 of pre-install.
5. **Verify.** `vectis status` plus a login at `https://mail.your-domain/admin`.

### Resource profile (v0.1.13+)

A `resources.profile` knob in `/etc/vectis/config.yaml` picks per-container
memory ceilings. Limits are hard cgroup ceilings — a service exceeding its
limit is OOM-killed by its own cgroup, never the whole host.

| Profile | Base | + Webmail+Obs | + ClamAV small | Suits |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| dev | ~1.8 GB | ~2.6 GB | ~3.6 GB | Laptop / 2 GB VPS |
| **small (default)** | ~3.5 GB | ~4.6 GB | ~6.1 GB | Single-domain 4 GB VPS |
| production | ~6.7 GB | ~8.0 GB | ~10 GB | Multi-domain 8 GB VPS |
| enterprise | ~13.5 GB | ~16.5 GB | ~19.5 GB | High-volume 16 GB+ |

To change: edit `resources.profile` in `/etc/vectis/config.yaml`, then
`vectis update apply`. Brief container restart picks up the new ceilings.

---

## REST API (overview)

Base URL: `https://mail.your-domain/api/v1`. Authentication is via
domain-scoped API keys (header `X-API-Key: <key>`) for the sending and
mailbox-CRUD paths; admin endpoints use a session cookie or super-admin
bearer token.

Endpoint groups (~60 endpoints total):

- **Domains** — `GET/POST/PATCH/DELETE /domains` — create, list, update,
  delete domains. DKIM key generation on create.
- **Mailboxes** — `GET/POST/PATCH/DELETE /mailboxes` — mailbox CRUD,
  password rotation, quota.
- **Aliases** — `GET/POST/PATCH/DELETE /aliases` — alias management with
  catch-all support.
- **Send** — `POST /send` — single send. `POST /send/batch` — batch send
  up to 100 messages.
- **Webhooks** — `GET/POST/PATCH/DELETE /webhooks` — outbound event webhooks.
  `GET /webhooks/deliveries` — delivery history.
- **Messages** — `GET /messages` — query metadata with filters; full-text
  search via `?q=`.
- **Analytics** (Pro) — `GET /analytics/{domain}` — per-domain delivery,
  bounce, complaint, engagement metrics.
- **Admin** — `GET /admin/users`, `POST /admin/users`, role management,
  audit log (`/audit`, super-admin only as of v0.1.13).
- **Health** — `GET /health` — container + dependency health.
- **License** — `GET /license` — current tier and entitlements.
- **Account** — `GET /account/billing` — generates a one-shot signed URL to
  the ValidonX billing portal.

### Sending example

```bash
curl -X POST https://mail.example.com/api/v1/send \
  -H "X-API-Key: $VECTIS_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "from": "alerts@example.com",
    "to": ["user@destination.example"],
    "subject": "Order confirmed",
    "text": "Plain-text body",
    "html": "<p>HTML body</p>"
  }'
```

### Inbound webhook example

Configure a webhook URL per domain. When mail arrives, Vectis POSTs:

```json
{
  "id": "msg_01HZ...",
  "received_at": "2026-05-17T10:00:00Z",
  "to": "support@example.com",
  "from": "customer@example.org",
  "subject": "Help needed",
  "text": "...",
  "html": "...",
  "attachments": [
    { "filename": "screenshot.png", "content_type": "image/png", "size": 12345, "url": "https://..." }
  ]
}
```

With header `X-Vectis-Signature: sha256=<HMAC of body>`. Retry policy:
exponential backoff up to 24 hours, then dead-letter to the messages table.

---

## CLI

The `vectis` command-line tool. Key commands:

- `vectis preflight` — pre-install system checks
- `vectis install` — initial deployment
- `vectis status` — current state (containers, version, license tier)
- `vectis update plan` — preview pending updates (image bumps, config diffs)
- `vectis update apply` — atomic apply with rollback on failure
- `vectis backup create` / `vectis backup restore` — manual backup/restore
- `vectis admin reset-password` — reset super-admin password from CLI
  (uses CLI auth, not API session)
- `vectis preflight cert-rotation` — verify cert-extractor reload pipeline
  before a renewal window

The CLI talks to the orchestrator on `http://localhost:8081` (bound to
127.0.0.1 only). No external port is exposed.

---

## License model

Vectis Mail is licensed under **Business Source License (BSL) 1.1** with a
4-year convert-to-Apache-2.0 clause per version. The full LICENSE file
lives at https://github.com/Veltara-Works/vectis/blob/main/LICENSE.

Key terms:

- **Source available immediately.** All code is in the public repository
  from day one.
- **Allowed use:** running Vectis Mail for your own organisation and your
  own end users, including operating mail for customers of your
  organisation as a feature of your own product.
- **Restricted use:** offering Vectis Mail itself as a hosted, embedded, or
  managed service to third parties in a way that competes with Veltara
  Works's paid versions. For this, contact licensing@veltaraworks.com.
- **Automatic Apache 2.0 conversion:** each version converts to Apache
  License 2.0 four years after its first public release. After a version's
  Change Date, anyone may fork, host, or relicense that version under
  Apache 2.0 — even for competing hosted offerings.

Pro features are gated by a license key issued by ValidonX. License
verification is offline-tolerant (works through your current paid period;
entitlements cached in Postgres).

## Vs alternatives — when to pick what

| Vs | Pick Vectis Mail when |
|---|---|
| **Mailcow** | You want the same self-hosted mail stack but with a declarative YAML config, REST API, and atomic update orchestrator instead of edit-files-and-pray + manual `mailcow.sh update`. |
| **iRedMail** | You want a modern Go control plane + React admin UI instead of the legacy PHP admin and shell-script management surface. |
| **Mail-in-a-Box** | You want production-shaped infrastructure (Docker, RBAC, atomic updates, MFA) instead of a single-script home-server setup. |
| **SendGrid / Postmark / Mailgun** | Your monthly bill is climbing past $200 and the per-email model feels misaligned with your costs. Vectis ships the same sending API and inbound webhook flow at a flat $0–29/month. |
| **Postal** | You want the same self-hosted SMTP-API split but with built-in webmail, IMAP/POP3, inbound email parsing, and one tool that does the whole mail server (not just outbound). |
